detail.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the Qwen4Exp QSA layer's main-attention QK-norm, RoPE, gate split and K/V cache write now run inside the fused QSA prepare launch, as #57097 did for NVIDIA.

## Claims

- MI355X TP2 `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`: +0.9% to +2.9% output throughput, faster in all 8 measured cells (4 points × 2 repeats).
- Accuracy neutral: GSM8K 0.9638 → 0.9605 over 6 pairs, a −0.33 point paired difference within run-to-run noise (paired t = −1.8, 5 df).
- Kernel numerics no worse than the unfused AMD chain against an fp64 reference; the gate is bit-identical.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (gfx950): 24 passed, 8 skipped.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py
```

- `test_qsa_prepare_amd.py` (renamed from `test_qsa_pre_indexer_amd.py`): in all 8 bf16 configurations, the indexer outputs match as before, and the main attention matches the AMD layer's unfused chain (split, Gemma RMSNorm, the layer's `rotary_emb`, `reshape_and_cache_flash`): Q and the paged K/V cache within bf16 tolerance, including MRoPE; the gate bit for bit, in the caller's buffer. The 8 FP8 cases skip: the AMD QSA caches are bf16-only.
- `test_qsa_amd.py`: the fused path passes the real tokens' `qkv`, `slot_mapping`, gate buffer, per-token cache view and norm weights; the unfused path never calls the kernel.
- Runs in the existing AMD `models_basic` step.

**Serving**, MI355X TP2, one-factor A/B against the same image without this change (#57947 in both arms), two repeats with the arms on rotated GPU pairs. `control → candidate`, mean of the repeats:

| ISL | OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Per repeat, tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 4 | 462.0 → 475.5 (+2.9%) | 7.39 → 7.12 (−3.7%) | +1.1% / +4.8% |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 16 | 964.1 → 975.3 (+1.2%) | 13.70 → 13.51 (−1.4%) | +1.4% / +1.0% |
| 8,192 | 1,024 | 64 | 1457.2 → 1471.0 (+0.9%) | 35.44 → 35.17 (−0.8%) | +1.4% / +0.5% |
| 60,000 | 600 | 4 | 144.8 → 147.4 (+1.8%) | 14.23 → 13.96 (−1.9%) | +0.8% / +2.7% |

```bash
# plus the checkpoint card's ROCm environment and flags, identical in both arms
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 128
```

**Accuracy**, GSM8K 5-shot on the checkpoint card's recipe (flexible-extract), 6 control/candidate pairs run side by side:

| pair | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| control | 0.9659 | 0.9674 | 0.9629 | 0.9621 | 0.9598 | 0.9644 | 0.9638 |
| candidate | 0.9560 | 0.9606 | 0.9636 | 0.9629 | 0.9553 | 0.9644 | 0.9605 |

One GSM8K run's standard error is about 0.005, so the per-pair differences (−1.0 to +0.1 points) sit within run-to-run noise.

<details>
<summary>Kernel numerics against fp64, 256 tokens at positions up to 200k, Flash-Next per-rank head counts</summary>

| | fused, max / mean abs error | unfused, max / mean abs error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main Q, text RoPE | 0.0296 / 0.00130 | 0.0411 / 0.00139 |
| main K, text RoPE | 0.0259 / 0.00127 | 0.0432 / 0.00134 |
| main Q, MRoPE | 0.0302 / 0.00124 | 0.0302 / 0.00132 |
| main K, MRoPE | 0.0200 / 0.00123 | 0.0287 / 0.00132 |

</details>

## Details

- **Kernel.** `amd/ops/qsa_pre_indexer.py` becomes `amd/ops/qsa_prepare.py`, matching NVIDIA's naming, and takes #57097's main-attention programs unchanged. Its only other difference from NVIDIA's kernel is still #57947's two-masked-load state select.
- **Gate out of the op.** The AMD layer applies the output gate after its opaque QSA op, so the gate has to come out of it. A new `qwen4_exp_qsa_prepare_with_output` custom op takes the packed `qkv` and mutates `output` and `gate`; the wrapper's optional `main_gate_out` writes the gate straight into that buffer.
- **Padding rows.** `* sigmoid(gate)` stays in the compiled graph, where Inductor fuses it as before. NVIDIA's attention kernel gates real tokens only; AMD's graph gates every row, so the op zeroes the gate's cudagraph-padding rows, keeping them at the zero output `forward_qsa` writes. With no padding the fill launches nothing.
- **Eligibility.** On when the layer has an output gate, the indexer passes `supports_fused_pre_indexer`, and the main head dim is a power of two. The main RoPE reads the indexer's cos/sin table, which is the layer's own `rotary_emb`. Otherwise both prepares take the unfused chain, as on NVIDIA.
- **No CPU/GPU sync** on the hot path: eligibility is decided at init; the gate padding size is the static difference between the padded and real token counts.

---

- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

The deviation is intended. NVIDIA's `use_fused_qsa_prepare` is `use_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate and indexer.use_fused_pre_indexer`, and `use_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate` is `attn_output_gate`, NeoX RoPE, `is_cuda()`, fp16/bf16 and `text_only or supports_mrope`. Term by term on AMD:

- NeoX RoPE and the MRoPE section: `supports_fused_pre_indexer` already requires both, so `indexer.use_fused_pre_indexer` covers them.
